newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 11.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 11.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT The right marketing strategy is increasingly making the difference between success or failure for financial services, board members and marketing leaders of a Volks-und Raifeisenbank conference conclude, SGZ Bank reports. Experts say financial services advertising must be presented with an emotional pull. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Advertising group Euro RSCG says it plans to consolidate its business in Germany into two agencies: Euro RSCG Werbeagentur and Euro RSCG Thomsen. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Sparda Bank in Nuremberg continues to expand and plans a new image and advertising campaign. (Handelsblatt)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - A dozen top companies in the German multimedia industry say they have formed their own watchdog organisation to keep their Internet services free of content considered indecent or illegal. The new group, Voluntary Self-Regulation of Multimedia Services, includes Microsoft, ProSieben Media and Deutsche Telekom. (Reuter)

BONN - The Bertelsmann group plans to conquer broader markets with its online services and boost its advertising revenues from the Internet, Bertelsmann multimedia director Bernd Schiphorst says. He says he is convinced that advertising can become an important source of financing for online services. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Pay TV Group Premiere says Ferdinand Kayser, a board member of European broadcasting group CLT/Ufa, has been appointed managing director. Kayser replaces Bernd Kundrun, who stepped down to run the newspaper division of Germany biggest magazine publisher, Gruner+Jahr, which is owned by Bertelsmann AG. (Reuter)
BONN - The new president of the Association of German Newspaper

Publishers (BVDZ), Hubert Burda, says the industry is under massive pressure. Stiffer competition, globalisation, the robust expansion of television and the fear of political reform are all influencing the newspaper market, Burda writes in a letter to BVDZ members. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MUNICH - Compaq Computer Corp says European sales in the second quarter rose 41 percent in unit terms and 21 percent in dollar values. "It was a very good quarter," Compaq European chief Andreas Barth says. "We had phenomenal unit growth." (Reuter)

SALZBURG - Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG says it has ended its six-year relationship with French software maker Cap Gemini in a deal that would have a substantial impact on 1997 earnings. Klaus Mangold, chief executive of Daimler services unit Debis, says Cap Gemini's holding company CGIP has agreed to buy the German group's 24.4 percent stake in Gemini for 1.4 billion marks ($798.4 million) in cash. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Insurer Allianz AG says it will not rule out withdrawing from the Ergo mega-merger announced last week. Allianz owns about 10 percent of Ergo as a result of its 20 percent stake in Hanburg-Mannheimer, a unit of rival Munich Re. Munich Re formed Ergo by merging its DKV and Hamburger-Mannnheimer with Victoria Holding AG. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - German industrial conglomerate Thyssen AG confirms it plans to hold talks with Preussag AG on cooperating in shipbuilding. Initial talks are planned for next week, with concrete negotiations due to start in the autumn, but the results are open, a Thyssen spokesman says. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Matthias Birkenbach, creative director of Scholz & Friends in Hamburg, has left for Stoehr Scheer in Duesseldorf. He succeeds Reinold Scheer, who left two years ago for Scholz & Friends. (Reuter)
